title: legacy MANIFEST `version` key stamped newer-than-supported is rejected (manifest-level companion to row 4)
why: The C++ HOST registry's manifest door
(host_registry.h::load) had NO schema_version gate at all — a manifest
with valid aether_abi + pattern and schema_version 99 passed every
manifest-level gate and failed only on the downstream sidecar file read,
while Python's load_manifest and the DEVICE registry both rejected it
naming the upgrade rule. This row pins the fix (host_registry.h now gates
on schema_version before the pattern/duplicate-id/format checks, mirroring
plugin_registry/registry.h:106) so a regression back to that hole fails
mechanically in both languages.
It also stamps the LEGACY `"version"` spelling rather than
`"schema_version"`, deliberately: C++ `parse_manifest` maps the legacy
key onto `m.schema_version` as a pre-existing fallback, and Python's
`check_schema_version(..., allow_legacy_version_key=True)` honors the
same fallback for manifests (registry.py `load_manifest`) — so this one
row pins BOTH this gate's closure AND the so-far-unpinned MANIFEST-half
of the legacy-`version`-key asymmetry (the fallback-honored direction;
row 16 already pins the SIDECAR-half, where the legacy key is ignored)
in both languages.
`pattern` is stamped a recognized, launch-certified value ("vector") so
this fixture isolates the schema_version gate — the pattern check sits
AFTER schema_version in both registries and is never reached here.
Shares row 4 with the sidecar-level `row04_schema_version_plus_one`
fixture (duplicate row numbers across fixtures at
different levels are permitted, per row02/row02b precedent); the
required-row floor is unaffected.
